title: Autoscaler hysteresis + topology staleness caused reserved-capacity gap and customer burst failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers experienced request failures and latency spikes during short bursts even though reserved pools appeared to have headroom. Investigation uncovered an interaction between aggressive autoscaler downscale behavior and stale topology information from the private agent mesh, which together delayed scale-up and exhausted burst credits.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated reserved pool with heterogeneous GPU types and tenant affinity tags
2) Generate a short 2-3 minute 3x traffic spike for several tenants to consume burst credits and increase KV cache pressure
3) Simulate a private-agent mesh partition to delay topology refresh beyond 30s
4) Observe reserved-pool headroom metrics, autoscaler decisions, and allocator leader slot counts
incident_timeline: 2026-03-01T01:12Z - Pager: multiple tenants reported 429/503; monitoring fired 'reserved-pool-exhausted' alerts for eu-west-1-dedicated-12
2026-03-01T01:20Z - On-call followed runbook; found queued requests and no scale-up events for ~48s while headroom fell
2026-03-01T01:35Z - Engineering discovered a recent downscale at 00:40Z and leader views diverged on slot counts
2026-03-01T02:05Z - Workaround: disabled aggressive downscale rule and manually injected +20% headroom; error rate reduced
2026-03-01T06:30Z - Post-incident analysis: topology refresh latency spike due to agent mesh partition; allocator double-counted available slots for ~70s
2026-03-02T09:00Z - Support sent interim customer communications; SLO credits issued to affected tenants
root_cause: Two concurrent issues: (A) downscale hysteresis too permissive allowed premature scale-down and gave false confidence in headroom recovery; (B) private-agent mesh partition produced stale topology snapshots and inconsistent allocator counts which masked actual capacity deficits. The combination led the autoscaler to delay scale-up during bursts.
immediate_mitigations: Hotfix: increase autoscaler conservative window from 30s to 120s for dedicated pools (deployed 2026-03-01 03:10Z)
Relax downscale aggressiveness for tenants with burst-priority labels
Manual pool replenishments for impacted customers and SLA credit application
Enable short-term routing fallback to hosted model variant when reserved headroom < 10%
long_term_fixes: Make allocator topology authoritative with majority-quorum validation before committing headroom accounting
Rewrite autoscaler decision logic to a two-window model: fast emergency scale-up and conservative scale-down; expose per-tenant tunables
Add topology-age signal to autoscaler input so it behaves conservatively when topology freshness < 60s
Enhance observability: per-tenant headroom heatmap and end-to-end burst credit telemetry
Add chaos E2E tests that simulate mesh partitions plus traffic spikes in CI
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): conservative-window change deployed to 3 canary clusters on 2026-03-01 and monitor for 48h
Phase 2 (safety): enable topology-age gating in canary on 2026-03-05
Phase 3 (durable): allocator quorum commit and autoscaler rewrite targeted for runtime-1.24 in 2026-Q2
Customer comms: prepare postmortem and targeted outreach with CS
qa_and_telemetry_changes: Dashboards: reserved-pool headroom time series with alert when headroom < 15% for >60s
Load-test: combined spike + partition scenarios added to canary pipeline
Smoke test: validate fallback to hosted route when reserved headroom fails
